Plex is my Netflix alternative. I've got a bandwidth cap that prevents me from online streaming, so instead I've used Plex to access all my stored TV shows and movies that I've pulled from DVDs. It steams them across my local network to one of Plex's many apps and I get to feel like I'm living in the 21st century. The added bonus is that I'm curating my own library, so I get to decide what's there.

I'm 100% serious. I don't have the bandwidth for netflix, much less pirating movies.
What's that process like? I've got a few DVDs of television shows I want to rip, but I don't know the first thing about getting around copy protection.

I use a pair of programs to do the copying. MakeMKV will pull the files straight from your DVDs as MPEG2 encoded MKV files. If that's all you need, then that's all you need to do. The downside is that the MPEG2 codec that DVDs use is pretty old and inefficient, so I use a program called "Handbrake" to convert the MPEG2 encoded files into MP4s, which run on pretty much anything and are much more efficient (about a quarter the file size, so I can fit more of them on a hard drive).

It's a little daunting at first, but the Plex forums have a lot of helpful information. I wish I would have looked there first, since I tried every DVD ripping program under the sun first, and eventually settled on MakeMKV+Handbrake, which is the exact combination they recommend on the Plex forums. Both programs are free, but MKV will require you to either buy a licence or keep plugging in a trial license every month or so.

It took some time and some learning, but what you're left with is a digital collection of your own DVD content that can be streamed across your network (or even online if you use Plex's subscription service). It can be more expensive to keep buying DVDs than Netflix is, but I like owning my own media and being able to curate my collection. And I don't have to worry about Netflix losing the rights to a specific show and removing it from their library.

Edit: I've picked up a few tips since starting out, and now I've got a pretty good process going. My desktop is fitted with three DVD drives so I can rip three discs at once, and once I have a good amount of MKVs pulled from the DVDs, I queue them all up in Handbrake and let them convert overnight. I end up with a stack of MP4s in the morning that I cut and paste into my Plex media folder. It took a few months to get everything added in, and now I'm only adding a handful of things at a time as new movies and shows release on DVD.
